note: The ladder is built from what the records already carry: facets.heat on a style, and the maker's own heat word on a bottle. Scoville appears only where somebody published a number.
title: How hot do you want it

rungs.label: None
rungs.say: Butter, garlic, cheese. Nothing in it bites.

rungs.label: Mild
rungs.say: Sweet, salty, smoky. Heat is somewhere in the room, not on the wing.

rungs.label: Medium
rungs.say: The default order almost everywhere, and the one Buffalo means.

rungs.label: Hot
rungs.say: You notice it between wings now, not just during.

rungs.label: Very hot
rungs.say: Cayenne paste in frying fat. Bread underneath for a reason.

scale_note: Scoville heat units come from a lab assay of capsaicin in dried material, and the article behind the scale says the number moves with seed, climate, soil and method. Every figure below is somebody's published measurement, lined up on one axis.

scale.note: the bottom of the published scale

scale.name: Jalapeño

scale.name: Cayenne pepper

scale.name: Ghost pepper
scale.note: 855,000 reported by India's Defence Research Laboratory in 2000; 1,041,427 in 2004

scale.name: Pepper X
scale.note: over 2.6 million — the top of the table

ladder.q: A jalapeño on a nacho is…
You order wings. The counter asks how hot.

a.t: Mild. I want to taste it.

ladder.q: There is a sauce on the menu with a name like a weapon.
Halfway through, your face is going.

results.say: Garlic parmesan is a real order and you should stop apologising for it.
Mild is a flavour choice. Lemon pepper and Old Bay are waiting for you.
Medium. The order Buffalo means when it says nothing at all.
Hot, and you order it on purpose. Jerk and Korean hot want a word.
Nashville is expecting you. Bring the bread.
